say.en: Insulin once came from the pancreas of slaughtered cattle and pigs, and some patients reacted badly to it. Today E. coli makes exact human insulin. In this lesson: Explain how Eli Lilly produced human insulin by rDNA technology.
Describe the first clinical gene therapy for ADA deficiency.

body.en: *Insulin* used for diabetes was earlier extracted from the pancreas of slaughtered cattle and pigs; this animal insulin caused some patients to develop allergy or other reactions to the foreign protein. Insulin consists of two short polypeptide chains, chain A and chain B, linked together by disulphide bridges. In mammals, including humans, insulin is synthesised as a pro-hormone (pro-insulin) that contains an extra stretch called the C peptide; the C peptide is absent in mature insulin and is removed during maturation. The main challenge was getting insulin assembled into a mature form. In 1983 Eli Lilly, an American company, prepared two DNA sequences corresponding to the A and B chains of human insulin and introduced them into plasmids of E. coli to produce the insulin chains separately. Chains A and B were then extracted and combined by creating disulphide bonds to form human insulin (humulin).

points.en: *Insulin*: chains A and B joined by disulphide bridges
Pro-*insulin* has an extra C peptide, removed in maturation
Eli Lilly, 1983: A and B chains made separately in E. coli, then joined

title.en: Insulin and blood glucose after a meal
title.kn: ಊಟದ ನಂತರ ಇನ್ಸುಲಿನ್ ಮತ್ತು ರಕ್ತದ ಗ್ಲೂಕೋಸ್

narration.en: After a meal glucose enters the blood; the pancreas releases insulin, which lets cells take glucose up, and the level returns to normal in about two hours. In a person with type 1 diabetes no insulin is made and glucose stays high. Injected insulin, made by E. coli carrying the human A and B chain genes (Eli Lilly, 1983), brings it down. A simplified model.
narration.kn: ಊಟದ ನಂತರ ಗ್ಲೂಕೋಸ್ ರಕ್ತ ಸೇರುತ್ತದೆ; ಮೇದೋಜೀರಕ ಗ್ರಂಥಿ ಇನ್ಸುಲಿನ್ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ ಮಾಡಿ ಕೋಶಗಳು ಗ್ಲೂಕೋಸ್ ಹೀರುವಂತೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ; ಸುಮಾರು ಎರಡು ಗಂಟೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮಟ್ಟ ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಟೈಪ್ 1 ಮಧುಮೇಹದಲ್ಲಿ ಇನ್ಸುಲಿನ್ ಇಲ್ಲದೆ ಗ್ಲೂಕೋಸ್ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗಿಯೇ ಇರುತ್ತದೆ. ಮಾನವ A ಮತ್ತು B ಸರಪಳಿ ಜೀನ್ ಹೊಂದಿದ E. coli ತಯಾರಿಸಿದ ಇನ್ಸುಲಿನ್ (ಎಲಿ ಲಿಲ್ಲಿ, 1983) ಚುಚ್ಚುಮದ್ದು ಅದನ್ನು ಇಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಸರಳ ಮಾದರಿ.

body.en: *Gene therapy* is a collection of methods that allows correction of a gene defect diagnosed in a child or embryo: genes are inserted into a person's cells and tissues to treat a disease, the normal gene compensating for the non-functional one. The first clinical gene therapy was given in 1990 to a 4-year-old girl with adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency. ADA is crucial for the immune system to function, and the disorder is caused by deletion of the gene for ADA. Some children can be cured by bone marrow transplantation; in others enzyme replacement therapy (injecting functional ADA) helps, but neither is completely curative. In gene therapy, lymphocytes from the patient's blood are grown in culture, a functional ADA cDNA is introduced into them using a retroviral vector, and the cells are returned to the patient. Because these cells are not immortal, the patient needs periodic infusions. If the gene isolated from marrow cells producing ADA is introduced into cells at early embryonic stages, it could be a permanent cure.

points.en: First clinical *gene therapy*: 1990, ADA deficiency, 4-year-old girl
Lymphocytes + functional ADA cDNA via retroviral vector
Not permanent: lymphocytes are not immortal
Permanent cure: introduce gene into early embryonic cells

problem.en: A child with ADA deficiency receives gene therapy using his own lymphocytes. Two years later his ADA level falls again. Explain why, and suggest what could give a permanent cure.

steps.en: The functional ADA cDNA was introduced into mature lymphocytes using a retroviral vector.
Lymphocytes are not immortal: as the engineered cells die, ADA production falls, so periodic infusions are needed.
If the ADA gene is introduced into cells at an early embryonic stage, all their descendant cells would carry it.

answer.en: Engineered lymphocytes have a limited life span; introducing the gene into early embryonic cells could give a permanent cure.

narration.en: Recap. Animal insulin caused allergies; human insulin is now made by rDNA technology. Insulin: chains A and B joined by disulphide bridges; C peptide removed. Eli Lilly (1983) made A and B chains separately in E. coli. First gene therapy (1990): ADA deficiency, retroviral vector, periodic infusions.
